caption: Earth spins once every 24 hours. What if it slowed down so much that a single day lasted 100 hours? At the equator, the ground would move at about 400 km/h instead of today's 1,670 km/h. You'd get roughly 50 hours of sunlight in a row, followed by about 50 hours of darkness, so days would get much hotter and nights much colder than anything we're used to. Your body clock runs on roughly 24 hours, so you'd probably end up sleeping several times in one "day". A slower spin also means a weaker Coriolis effect, the force that makes cyclones spin. And here's the twist: Earth really is slowing down. Tidal friction from the Moon adds roughly 2 milliseconds to the length of a day every century. At that rate, 100-hour days are more than 10 billion years away, and the Sun has only about 5 billion years left. What would YOU do with 100 hours in a day? 👇
